hypotheses.title: CFG creation is O(N^2) on an if/else-if chain where every branch returns (pruneEmptyBlocks removes one empty join block per round)
hypotheses.issue: In semantics/internal/cfg/control_flow_analyzer.go, analyzeIf always returns continueEffect(finally), even when both branches are terminal. In a nested else-if chain, each inner join block (`finally`) gets an edge to the outer join block. When every branch returns, including the final else, this produces a chain of N empty join blocks, and only the innermost has no parent. pruneEmptyBlocks then loops `for {}`, calling findEmptyBlocks and removeBlocksAndReindex. isEmpty() is `id != 0 && len(parents)==0 && len(nodes)==0`, so each round removes exactly one block: the next block in the chain loses its last parent only after the reindex. That gives N rounds. Each round scans every block, builds two fresh maps (removeSet, oldToNew), copies every basicBlock struct into a new slice that is not pre-sized, and reallocates every block's parent and child slices (remapRefs). The total is O(N^2) copying and allocation plus GC. With 3000 branches, CFG creation takes about 7.6 s of a 9.2 s compile. The same chain with a trailing `return` instead of a final `else` takes 10 ms. Profile at N=2000: removeBlocksAndReindex is 38% of all CPU, and the `newBbs = append(newBbs, bb)` line alone takes 1.25 s. Scaling of CFG creation: N=500 170 ms, 1000 705 ms, 2000 2.9 s, 3000 7.4 s, 4000 13.1 s. This is a realistic shape: string or enum dispatchers written as if / else-if return chains.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Usage: gen.py [N] [--no-else]
# Generates a dispatcher function: an if / else-if chain where every branch
# (including the final else) returns. CFG pruneEmptyBlocks then needs one
# full prune+reindex round per chain level -> O(N^2) CFG creation.
# --no-else emits the same chain with a trailing `return -1;` instead of a
# final else (control case: the cascade does not happen).
import sys
args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
n = int(args[0]) if args else 3000
no_else = "--no-else" in sys.argv
o = ["import ballerina/io;", "", "function code(string s) returns int {"]
o.append('    if s == "k0" {\n        return 0;\n    }')
for i in range(1, n):
    o.append(f'    else if s == "k{i}" {{\n        return {i};\n    }}')
if no_else:
    o.append("    return -1;\n}\n")
else:
    o.append("    else {\n        return -1;\n    }\n}\n")
o.append('public function main() {\n    io:println(code("k7"));\n}')
print("\n".join(o))
reproducer.command: python3 gen.py 3000 > repro.bal; go build -o bal ./cli/cmd; ./bal run --stats repro.bal  (read the user module's Analysis > CFG Creation). Control: python3 gen.py 3000 --no-else. Benchmark: ./bin/benchmark --mode time|memory --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> repro.bal

hypotheses.fix_approach: pruneEmptyBlocks now removes every transitively empty block in a single worklist pass. It seeds the worklist with findEmptyBlocks and marks those blocks in a dense `removed []bool`. For each popped block it calls removeParent on each child; if the child is now empty and not yet marked, it is marked and pushed. It then reindexes once. removeBlocksAndReindex takes the bool mask and uses a dense `oldToNew []int` (-1 means removed) instead of the two maps, and pre-sizes newBbs to len(bbs). remapRefs uses the dense slice. The removal set is the same transitive closure the round-based loop reached, kept blocks keep their relative order, and edge filtering preserves order, so the CFG is identical: no corpus/cfg goldens changed and make test passes. markBackedges runs after pruning, so back-edges are unaffected. Pitfall: the root cause is that analyzeIf builds a join block even when both branches are terminal. Returning a terminal effect there would avoid building the chain at all, but it changes the CFG shape and therefore the goldens, so the prototype only fixed the prune cost. Separately, the fix agent observed that deeply nested (non-chain) if/else is still mildly superlinear in another stage; this was not investigated.

notes: Other leads seen during exploration but not pursued: (1) a union of 1000-2000 distinct record types makes top-level type resolution quadratic (bddUnionWithMemo / internBddNodeKey rebuilding the BDD chain on each fold, plus memo-map rehash), 0.49 s at 1000 and 2.2 s at 2000; (2) symbol resolution takes about 1 s on the 3000-branch chain in both the repro and the control, likely the previously reported blockSymbolResolver parent-chain issue.
